title: The Request the Server Made
description:
Tunde: 'The IAM credentials were not stolen through the front end. The admin panel had an import feature — submit a URL and the server fetches the content on your behalf. This is where the breach became a full infrastructure compromise.'

Amaka: 'The network capture shows the server making an outbound HTTP request to an address that is only reachable from within the cloud instance itself — a link-local range cloud providers reserve for a service that hands back instance metadata to whatever is running on the box. The Griot knew which exact endpoint to hit on that service to surface the IAM role credentials. Look it up if you don't know it offhand — knowing what to type into that field is half the skill.'

Reconstruct the request The Griot made to the import form. The simulated server will respond the same way the production server did.

In the pentest finding (task 9) you will be asked to name this class precisely, what the cloud-side mitigation is (the v2 of the same metadata service), and one architectural control beyond "validate the input" that would have stopped it. Take notes on the metadata endpoint path and the IAM role you saw in the response.

Reference: OWASP Top 10 2021 A10 Server-Side Request Forgery; CWE-918 (SSRF); MITRE ATT&CK T1190; AWS IMDSv2 documentation (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configuring-instance-metadata-service.html).
